column1: # Every code-versioned `State`, versioned by the code that derives its
# value rather than by the release. Columns: namespace, version,
# comma-separated sources whose text produces the stored bytes (the
# owning crate's file first; an entry ending `/` names every file under
# that tree, so a new file in a listed tree fails the guard too),
# comma-separated Cargo.lock packages whose locked versions the
# derivation's bytes depend on (`-` when none), and the sha256 of all of
# it (each file as `path\0bytes\0`, each package as `name\0versions\0`).
# A tree's files hash in component-wise path order, so a directory sorts
# before the file whose name it prefixes (`pypi/settings.rs` before
# `pypi.rs`).
# The version lives at the `State::VERSION` beside `CODE_VERSIONED`; the
# parity test in the owning crate (state_parity, or the crate's
# derive_parity module) checks this table and that every `CODE_VERSIONED`
# impl in the crate's sources is registered. When a state's source — or
# one of its listed dependencies' locked versions — changes, the test
# fails naming the new hash: bump the version and update this row in the
# same commit. A row must list every file the derivation reads bytes
# through; whole files and trees are hashed, so a formatting or comment
# edit in a listed file also needs the bump (batch cosmetic edits in
# these files). Over-include rather than miss: when in doubt, list the
# whole tree. Every `impl State` in non-test workspace source is either a
# row here or an entry in tests/state-exempt.tsv; the coverage check in
# the parity test fails on a state that is neither, on a listing whose
# impl is gone, and on a flag that disagrees with the table.
